issue.standard_remedy: Map the sub-tier and qualify an alternate
issue.summary: Depends on a single-source sub-tier supplier (Europe)

plan.diagnosis: Dynamo Northern Components KG (Germany) represents a single-source sub-tier dependency with USD 1,955,608 annual spend and 35 sub-tier suppliers, creating supply chain visibility and continuity risk despite a moderate resiliency score of 63 and zero disruption events in the past 12 months. The concentration risk is compounded by limited transparency into the 35-supplier sub-tier network, preventing proactive risk mitigation. While the Europe geographic region and stable disruption history provide some comfort, the lack of alternate sourcing options exposes USD 1.96M in annual spend to potential sub-tier failures.

remedy_steps.step: Conduct sub-tier mapping exercise with Dynamo Northern Components KG to identify critical suppliers among the 35 sub-tier vendors, focusing on components representing >10% of our USD 1,955,608 spend
Issue RFI to 3-5 alternative European component suppliers with comparable sub-tier networks to assess technical capability, capacity, and willingness to serve as secondary source
Negotiate contractual sub-tier transparency clause with Dynamo requiring quarterly disclosure of critical sub-suppliers and 30-day advance notice of sub-tier changes
Qualify and onboard one alternate supplier for 20-30% of current Dynamo scope (targeting USD 390,000-590,000), prioritizing highest-risk component families identified in sub-tier mapping
Implement dual-source purchase order allocation strategy and establish safety stock buffer equivalent to 4-6 weeks demand for critical components

plan.expected_impact: Mitigating single-source sub-tier risk through dual sourcing and enhanced visibility will protect USD 1,955,608 in annual spend from potential sub-tier disruptions and improve supply continuity for dependent manufacturing operations.
kpis: Sub-tier supplier visibility: map 100% of critical sub-tier suppliers (target: top 80% of Dynamo's spend) within 30 days
Alternate supplier qualification: onboard 1 qualified secondary source within 120 days
Spend diversification: achieve 20-30% allocation to alternate supplier (USD 390,000-590,000) within 180 days
Supply continuity: establish 4-6 weeks safety stock buffer for critical components
Contractual compliance: secure sub-tier transparency clause with quarterly reporting requirements
risks: Dynamo Northern Components KG may resist sub-tier disclosure due to competitive concerns, delaying visibility into the 35-supplier network
Alternate supplier qualification timeline may extend beyond 120 days if technical requirements or quality standards prove difficult to meet
Splitting USD 1,955,608 spend across multiple sources may reduce volume leverage and increase piece-price by 5-8%
Incumbent supplier relationship strain if Dynamo perceives dual-sourcing as lack of partnership commitment
New supplier ramp-up quality issues could disrupt production during 20-30% volume transfer
Sub-tier mapping may reveal deeper dependencies or single-source raw material constraints beyond Dynamo's control
erp_actions: SAP: Create source list entries (ME01) for alternate supplier once qualified, with quota arrangement allocating 70-80% to Dynamo (supplier block released) and 20-30% to new source
SAP: Update info records (ME11) for both suppliers with lead times and minimum order quantities based on sub-tier constraints identified in mapping
Coupa: Add Dynamo Northern Components KG to enhanced monitoring supplier segment requiring quarterly sub-tier risk attestation and supplier relationship management reviews
SAP: Configure safety stock levels (MD04) for critical component SKUs to 4-6 weeks demand in material master (MM02)
Oracle EBS/Dynamics 365/NetSuite: Create approved supplier list entries for alternate source across all ERP instances to enable cross-plant sourcing flexibility
Coupa: Implement contract workspace for Dynamo with sub-tier transparency clause and milestone tracking for quarterly sub-tier supplier disclosure submissions
SAP: Set purchasing info record (MEK1) validity periods to trigger buyer review 90 days before contract renewal to reassess sub-tier risk and source allocation
